commits.messageBody:
Migration 005 adds the tables for CF-05 and CF-08 to CF-20 ahead of their
services: status history, coordinator assignments, venues and their blocked
periods, venue bookings, pooled equipment types and requests, attendee
registrations, change requests and notifications. It also allows the later
CONFIRMED, CANCELLED and COMPLETED request statuses and adds the registration
capacity and window to event_requests.

Triggers guard only the invariants concurrent requests could otherwise break:
the status-history record, one approved booking per venue and period, the
pooled equipment peak and the registration capacity. Roles, ownership and
transition validity stay with the services.

Migration 006 corrects 005's equipment guard, which summed every overlapping
reservation instead of taking the simultaneous peak and so refused requests
that never coincide.

New tables keep migration 002's Data API boundary: row-level security on, no
privileges for the Supabase API roles, and a pinned search_path on each
trigger function.

The rules for Q-04 and Q-06 to Q-13 are provisional team assumptions recorded
in database/README.md; revise them through new migrations once the customer
answers.

commits.messageBody:
POST /api/events creates a DRAFT owned by the verified organiser, taking
organiser_id from the session and never from the body. It accepts the same
optional partial draft that PATCH validates and returns the same flat event
shape.

The draft input now also carries the CF-18 registration settings
(registrationCapacity, registrationOpensAt, registrationClosesAt) as an
extension type, because EventDraftFields is frozen, and rejects counts above
PostgreSQL's integer limit rather than failing the write with a 500. The
shared detail read returns those settings so the edit page can load them.

NewEventPage replaces its placeholder with the real form: every event field
in Singapore time, first save creates and later saves PATCH only what
changed, submit saves first and then shows any missingFields beside the
right inputs. EditDraftPage resumes an owned draft and refuses one that is
no longer editable. The organiser detail page gains Edit draft and Submit
for review while the request is a DRAFT the caller owns.

commits.messageHeadline: feat(KAN-31,KAN-4,KAN-34): create, save and edit event request drafts

commits.messageBody:
…equests and lifecycle

Assignment (CF-05) lets a coordinator list unassigned non-draft requests and
the coordinator directory, take or hand over a request, and read its
assignment history. Assigning updates event_requests.coordinator_id and the
active coordinator_assignments row in one transaction; only the currently
assigned coordinator may hand over.

Clarifications (CF-04, KAN-27) let the assigned coordinator ask a question
from SUBMITTED or UNDER_REVIEW, moving the request to
CLARIFICATION_REQUESTED, and the owning organiser answer it, returning the
request to SUBMITTED once nothing is outstanding. A coordinator can also
mark a request as under review.

Review eligibility now accepts a decision from UNDER_REVIEW as well as
SUBMITTED. Without this, marking a request as under review left the
coordinator unable to approve or reject it except by a clarification
round-trip. A pending clarification still blocks a decision.

Change requests (CF-19) let the owner propose field changes to an APPROVED
or CONFIRMED event with a reason, reusing the draft input rules. Approval
applies the changes and, where the date or attendance really differs,
cancels that event's bookings and equipment reservations so the
arrangements are re-requested.

Lifecycle (CF-06, CF-12) adds confirm, cancel and complete with their
preconditions, plus the status-history read.

Every write runs in one transaction that sets app.actor_id for the
status-history trigger and locks the event row, and notifies the affected
organiser, coordinator and attendees but never the actor. The provisional
rules for Q-02, Q-04, Q-05, Q-11 and Q-12 are in each service's header.

commits.messageBody:
…ing and approval

Venue staff maintain the catalogue (CF-08) and block periods for
maintenance; any signed-in user can search and filter it by capacity,
facilities, accessibility features, layout and a free period (CF-10), and
read a venue's availability calendar (CF-09). Other people's event names
stay hidden from organisers and attendees.

Suitability (CF-11) reports capacity, accessibility, operating hours,
availability and active checks. Per the provisional Q-08 rule an unsuitable
venue can still be booked; the failed checks travel with the request and are
shown to venue staff when they decide.

Organisers and assigned coordinators request a booking for an APPROVED or
CONFIRMED event (CF-12); venue staff approve or reject it (CF-13). Pending
requests do not hold a slot, so conflicts surface at approval: the database
raises 23P01 and the service maps it to 409 VENUE_BOOKING_CONFLICT or
VENUE_UNAVAILABLE with the conflicting intervals (CF-14). An integration
test parks two overlapping approvals behind the venue row lock and asserts
exactly one succeeds.

commits.messageHeadline: feat(KAN-8,KAN-12,KAN-21,KAN-28): venue catalogue, availability, book…

commits.messageBody:
…rvation

Equipment is pooled by type with a total quantity, the provisional Q-09
rule. Technical support staff maintain the catalogue and cannot lower a
total below the peak already reserved.

Availability (CF-16) reports the maximum simultaneous reserved quantity in a
window, computed by a sweep over the reservation boundaries rather than a
plain sum, so reservations that never coincide do not appear to consume the
same units.

Organisers and assigned coordinators request equipment for an APPROVED or
CONFIRMED event (CF-15); technical support staff reserve or reject it
(CF-17) from a queue that shows the quantity actually available for that
window. The database guard raises 23P01 when a reservation would exceed the
pool and the service maps it to 409 EQUIPMENT_UNAVAILABLE with the
available quantity. An integration test holds two reservations that together
exceed the pool behind the type row lock and asserts exactly one succeeds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: feat(KAN-9,KAN-18,KAN-26): equipment catalogue, availability and rese…

commits.messageBody:
…tions

Registration (CF-18) exposes discoverable events to any signed-in user with
public fields only, never the organiser and coordinator ids, internal
requirements or review data. An event is open when it is APPROVED or
CONFIRMED, marks registration required, is inside its window, has not
started and has room; a NULL capacity means unlimited. These are the
provisional Q-10 rules.

Attendees register and withdraw, and re-registering after a withdrawal
reuses the existing row so the unique attendee-and-event pair holds. The
capacity trigger raises 23P01 and the service maps it to 409
REGISTRATION_FULL; an integration test fires two simultaneous registrations
at a capacity of one and asserts exactly one succeeds. Only the owning
organiser and the assigned coordinator can read the attendee list.

Notifications (CF-20) are in-app with read state and no delivery retry, the
provisional Q-13 rule. notify() takes the caller's transaction client so a
notification is saved only when the action it describes commits, and
de-duplicates recipients. The inbox is keyset paginated by created_at and
id so rows sharing a timestamp are not skipped, and a bell polls the unread
count only while signed in and visible.

title: KAN-24: first-release database schema, ERD, and the services and pages that use them

commits.messageBody:
KAN-24 was "set up the database infrastructure required to persist the
information needed by the Sprint 1 user stories and generate database
diagram". PR #10 went far past that and shipped whole feature areas whose
Jira items were never in the Sprint 1 commitment and are still unassigned.
This removes the parts nothing else depends on.

Removed, roughly 15,000 lines:

- Venues (CF-08 to CF-14) - catalogue, availability, suitability, bookings
  and the conflict handling, backend and frontend.
- Equipment (CF-15 to CF-17) - types, peak availability and reservations.
- Registrations (CF-18) - discovery, register/withdraw and attendee lists.
- Notifications (CF-20) - the router, inbox page and bell. The notify()
  helper stays because the clarification and lifecycle services call it.
- Change requests (CF-19) - service, router and panel.
- Their routes, navigation, planning panels and documentation claims.

Kept, because main now depends on it. Six days of teammate work landed on
top of PR #10 and removing these breaks the build or their tests:

- EventRequestForm and the registration draft fields. PR #18 rewrote
  EventDraftEditPage to use the form, deleting 433 lines of its own.
- Coordinator assignment (CF-05). A teammate's ReviewAccessPage and its
  tests read /api/events/unassigned and /coordinators, and review-access
  .spec.ts asserts the "Unassigned requests" nav link exists.
- Clarifications (CF-04) and lifecycle/status history (CF-06). The same
  browser spec asserts that opening /reviews/:id fires reads for
  assignments, coordinators, clarifications and history, so those panels
  must stay mounted on the coordinator page.
- A decision from UNDER_REVIEW, which a teammate re-landed in c680051.
- Migrations 005 and 006, the ERD and docs/database-diagram.md. These are
  KAN-24's own deliverable, and both migrations are already applied to the
  shared Supabase project, so deleting the files would leave CI building a
  schema the live database does not match.

workflow-routers.test.ts and workflow-support.test.ts are trimmed to the
services that remain. workspace-fixtures.ts stays because a teammate's
review-access.spec.ts imports it.

Verified on this branch: typecheck clean, 190 frontend and 372 backend
tests, 119 PostgreSQL integration tests, 32 browser tests, both builds.
